question: Marcus has read 72 pages of his summer reading book by Monday. On Tuesday, he reads 70 more pages during a long car ride. On Wednesday, he reads 47 more pages before bed. A dozen kids in his class are doing the same reading challenge, though that number has nothing to do with his own page count. On Thursday, he reads 65 more pages during a rainy afternoon. On Friday, he skips 30 pages of an appendix section he doesn't need for his book report. A weekend re-reading of key chapters brings his effective page count to 6 times what it had been. How many pages has Marcus read now?

A hospital laundry had 71 rolls of paper towel, and a supplier delivered 63 more. Each roll was cut into 9 packs. A ward then took 496 packs. The trust ordered 4 packs for every pack still in the store. Half of the store is refrigerated, and the trust bills its supplies in dollars although the invoices are itemised in cents. How many packs does the order come to?

Two farmers, Ben and Lisa, track livestock. Ben has 170 cattle. He doubled his herd through breeding. Then he multiplied by 6 more. He added 72 from a purchase. This total was multiplied by 5. Then multiplied by 3 more for a census count. By comparison with Lisa's smaller herd, what was Ben's final count?

A grain depot began the week with 217 sacks. A farm delivered 26 more, a second farm sent 21, and a co-operative added 24. Every sack in the depot weighs 7 kilograms. The whole stock was then divided equally between 4 village shops, and the Bridge Street shop took the first share. How many kilograms of grain went to the Bridge Street shop?

Two rival breweries compared barrel counts. Oakwood Brewery had 206 barrels aging, even though the cellar has a dozen sections. Five more matching cellars joined, making the total six times as large. A shipment removed 263 barrels for a big order. Seven more matching cellars joined, making it eight times as large. Three more matching cellars made it four times as large. Finally, five more matching cellars made it six times as large, leaving Oakwood far ahead of the rival Pinehill Brewery's 9,000 barrels. How many barrels did Oakwood Brewery end up with?

A factory produced 81 toy robots in the first hour, tracked over 60 minutes, or 1 hour, of the shift. Two more matching hours tripled the total. Five more matching hours made it six times as large. Six more matching hours made it seven times as large. Finally, five more matching hours made it six times as large. How many toy robots did the factory produce in total?

Lee and Pat count inventory. They start with 146 units. They multiply by 4 (584). They lose 101 (483). They lose 139 (344). They divide by 2 (172). They double (344). Pat has 300. One distractor: the old price was 89. How many units do they count?

Jake's lemonade stand cash box held $148 at the start of the day. A neighboring stand collected a stray $20 bill that a customer meant for napkins, so that money never touched Jake's box. During the morning rush the box grew by $46, then by another $26 from the after-school crowd, and by $34 more from a big group order. Before closing, a good-sales-day bonus turned every dollar in the box into 4 dollars. Right after that, a local business match program turned every dollar into 8 dollars. How much money was in Jake's cash box after the business match program finished?

A garden project begins with 181 seeds. In the morning, they plant 37 more seeds. By afternoon, they receive 64 additional seeds. By evening, they prepare for multiplication, so they multiply by 4. They then divide the total among 6 garden beds. How many seeds go in each bed?

A bakery had 50 batches. They multiplied by 3 for morning production. Then by 7 for daily total. They added 15 more batches. They multiplied by 4 for a week's projection. Finally, 1891 batches from a large contract were subtracted. Using 'a dozen' as a measure, how many batches does the bakery track?

Hamid had logged 67 minutes of violin practice on Monday. He moved a full hour, which is 60 minutes, into his lesson log, and the remainder became his free-practice log. On Tuesday he added 55 minutes to the free-practice log, then his teacher reclassified 51 of those minutes as a lesson, and 2 minutes were struck out for a timing error. His sister Laila's free-practice log shows more minutes than Hamid's. How many minutes are on Hamid's free-practice log?

Two supervisors, Alex and Maria, manage equipment. Alex had 185 items. She removed 95. This was doubled. She added 45. This was multiplied by 4. She added 26. Maria tracked fewer. What was Alex's total?

Mateo tracked the total dollars in his skateboard fund, starting with 142 dollars saved. His friend Diego, by comparison, had saved a mere half of that in his own separate fund, but only Mateo's fund is tracked here. A parking fee mishap cost Mateo 1 dollar. A birthday gift added 25 dollars. A big purchase of new wheels then cost 147 dollars from the tracked fund. Finally, a summer job quadrupled whatever remained in the fund. How much money was in Mateo's skateboard fund after the summer job?

A bakery starts with 174 loaves. It adds 56 (230). It multiplies by 8 (1840). It multiplies by 6 (11040). It multiplies by 2 (22080). One distractor: previous stock was 95. How many loaves does it produce?

Two farmers, Odette and Kwame, store grain, but this story follows only Odette's bin, which started at 186 bushels, more than Kwame's bin held. A harvest added 52 more bushels, and a second field added 37 more. A large sale then used up 225 bushels, after a loading run that took about 60 minutes, exactly 1 hour. A neighbor's delivery added 46 more bushels, and a co-op added 57 more, around the time a rival farm reported storing 900 bushels, unrelated to this count. Finally, 22 more bushels arrived from a late harvest. How many bushels were in Odette's bin in the end?

A running club's charity fund stood at 210 pounds at the start of the month. A bake sale added 39 pounds and a car wash brought in 23. A member's sponsored run raised 43 pounds, and a quiz night added 40 more. A local firm then donated 78 pounds to the same fund. A collection tin in the clubhouse held a final 10 pounds. The club has a dozen junior members and 85 seniors. How many pounds are in the fund now?

In the morning, a warehouse had 39 boxes. By afternoon, 32 boxes were removed. By evening, they increased 7 times. They increased 5 times. They increased 6 times. Finally, they added 57 boxes. How many boxes do they have?

Two chess rivals compared their tournament points. Sasha had 130 points to start the season. She lost 5 points after a forfeited match. A club bonus, with three matching contributions, made her total four times as large. A rematch bonus then doubled her total. She earned 9 more points from a practice match. Finally, a season-ending championship made her total nine times as large, far ahead of her rival Petra, who only had 900 points. How many points did Sasha end up with?
A store had 208 items. They multiplied by 8. There was a loss of 1326 items. They lost 241 more. They had a distractor count of 75 items. They added 31. How many remain?

A single beehive started spring with 54 worker bees. A cold snap cost the colony 8 bees. A warm spell then added 41 more bees. A strong nectar season left the hive with 9 times as many bees. A swarm split then cost the hive 741 bees. Finally, 3 more bees returned from a scouting trip, around the time a neighboring hive was said to hold about a dozen queen cells, unrelated to this count. How many bees were in the hive in the end?

A council had 169 street lamps on the high street and removed 125 old ones. It installed 48 new lamps and put 22 more along the alley. Each lamp holds 4 bulbs. Every bulb uses 9 watts, and the council reports its use in watts rather than in kilowatts. The high street is 700 metres long. How many watts do the lamps use?

On Saturday morning a market trader had 202 toy cars on his stall, and 11 of them were sold early on. A collector returned 6 cars that were the wrong model. At midday a wholesaler matched the stall exactly, leaving 2 cars for every car on it. In the afternoon a house clearance added 76 cars, and 125 cars were sold before closing. In the evening the wholesaler supplied 9 cars for every car left on the stall. How many cars does the trader have now?
A business had 236 dollars. They removed 203 dollars. They multiplied by 4 times. They removed 125 dollars. They removed 4 dollars. The account progressed from opening to closing. How much money?

Rosa's bank account held 81 dollars. She paid 33 dollars for a phone bill, then deposited 40 dollars from a shift at the cafe. Her brother repaid 62 dollars he owed her, she sold an old lamp for 17 dollars, and her grandmother sent 15 dollars, all of which went into the account. Rosa tracks the account in dollars, though she knows a hundred cents make a dollar. How many dollars are in Rosa's account now?

Aiden read 47 pages of a novel on Monday, 6 pages on Tuesday and 49 pages on Wednesday. He read 27 pages on Thursday and 76 pages on Friday. The novel is divided into 12 chapters. All of the pages he had read were then divided equally among the 5 members of his book club, so that each member could summarise one stretch of the story. Aiden's own stretch was photocopied 6 times so that everyone could follow along. The club records its reading time in minutes rather than in hours. How many photocopied pages did Aiden's stretch produce?
